paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Hiding sin makes you miserable, and bringing it to the LORD sets you free. David kept silent and says, "my bones became brittle from my groaning all day long" (Psalm 32:3). Then he acknowledged his sin, and the LORD "forgave the guilt of my sin" (Psalm 32:5). The blessing was never for people who have no sin to bring. It's for the ones who bring it (Psalm 32:1).

So what do you do with that today? Don't carry it around like a cookie tray you're too embarrassed to set down! David says the LORD is "my hiding place," and that He surrounds him "with songs of deliverance" (Psalm 32:7). You don't have to hide FROM God, baker. You get to hide IN Him.

And then the psalm leans in with a promise: "I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go" (Psalm 32:8). So don't be stubborn like the horse or mule that has to be dragged along (Psalm 32:9). Come when He calls, because "loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD" (Psalm 32:10). That's why David ends the way he does: "Be glad in the LORD and rejoice" (Psalm 32:11). I'm still dabbing my eyes with my mustache over that one.
